author: Zuhayr Rahman Chowdhury
competitive_advantage: the largest connected fleet feeding self-driving data, plus high-volume integrated manufacturing.

statements.define: For tech-forward, mid-to-upper income EV buyers, plus utilities needing storage, Tesla offers software-defined cars that improve over time and charge easily.
statements.create: Tesla wins mainly on lower cost against legacy automakers, with WTP from software and charging. Against BYD it is neither cheapest nor premium: a temporary advantage.
statements.capture: EVs are a price war: rivalry and buyers take most value (deliveries -9% in 2025; BYD sold 2.25M BEVs). Direct sales, charging and FSD subscriptions protect some margin.
statements.deliver: Software, gigafactories, direct sales and Superchargers reinforce each other: more cars, more data, more FSD revenue. Tesla refuses dealers, broad model ranges and advertising.

one_line: Tesla is becoming a low-cost producer plus autonomy platform; watch FSD revenue versus margin erosion.

who: Tech-forward, mid-to-upper income EV buyers in the U.S., China and Europe; B2C: the driver uses, decides and pays
B2B: utilities and businesses buying Megapack storage (procurement decides, utility pays)
what: Hired to give a car that gets better through software, with easy fast charging, at a competitive price
Today they use gas cars and hybrids (Toyota), legacy EVs (VW, Hyundai, GM) or Chinese EVs (BYD, Xiaomi)
problem: Gas cars cost more to run; many EVs have weak software and patchy charging
Tesla closes the gap with over-the-air updates, Full Self-Driving and the largest North American fast-charging network
define.takeaway: Weakest premise: that buyers keep paying for software (FSD) as cheaper EVs flood the market.

wtp_vs_cost: **Moves WTP:** FSD and software updates, Supercharger convenience, performance
**Table stakes:** range, safety ratings, a modern screen
**Cost levers:** gigafactory scale, gigacasting, own batteries, no dealers
**Wedge:** lower cost vs legacy makers: 18.0% gross margin (2025)
map_reading: Axes: software and charging experience vs price
Buyers pick Tesla for software and charging
BYD on the frontier at lower cost; Ford and GM inside
create.takeaway: A cost position with a software kicker, squeezed by BYD.

vri.resource: Software and fleet-data loop (FSD, OTA updates)
vri.v: Yes: FSD subscriptions (1.48M) and robotaxi option
vri.r: Yes: largest camera fleet collecting driving data
vri.i: Hard: data feedback loop compounds; Waymo leads driverless rides
vri.verdict: Temporary, sustained if autonomy proves out

vri.v: Yes: lower unit cost lets it cut prices profitably
vri.i: Hard for legacy makers; Chinese rivals match
vri.verdict: Temporary advantage vs legacy; parity vs BYD

vri.r: Fading: rivals now plug in via NACS
vri.i: Costly to build, but access is now shared
vri.verdict: Now a capture asset (fees), not a WTP edge

create.vri_takeaway: Manufacturing scale is being matched in China; the durable edge depends on the software loop paying off.

forces.logic: Many EV options, easy comparison, and the end of the U.S. EV tax credit raise price sensitivity; more rivals and cheap Chinese EVs push buyer power up. Forces price cuts that compress margins.
forces.firm_power: Partly: software, FSD and charging lock in some owners; direct sales control price, but deliveries fell 9%

forces.logic: Cell makers (CATL, Panasonic, LG) are concentrated and key; China dominates materials, and tariffs add cost. Fragmented automakers raise supplier power; in-house cells lower it.
forces.firm_power: Partly: scale contracts and in-house 4680 cells give leverage legacy rivals lack

forces.logic: BYD (2.25M BEVs vs Tesla's 1.63M), Xiaomi, VW and Hyundai fight on price in China and Europe; price wars erode margins.
forces.firm_power: Partly: lower cost than legacy makers; no edge on cost vs BYD

forces.logic: Chinese tech firms enter fast using China's supply chain; capital and scale still deter most.
forces.firm_power: Yes vs most entrants: scale and brand

forces.logic: Hybrids and gas cars, and robotaxi services (Waymo) for not owning a car at all.
forces.firm_power: Partly: robotaxi is Tesla's own bet on the substitute

forces.logic: Charging and electricity prices shape EV value; NACS made Tesla the charging complement others pay.
forces.firm_power: Yes: owns the largest North American fast-charging network

capture.takeaway: Rivalry and buyers take most of the value in EVs; Tesla's escape route is software revenue that buyers can't get elsewhere.

deliver.statement: In-house software, integrated gigafactories, direct sales and Superchargers form one software-and-scale system that serves tech-forward buyers, cuts cost, and earns subscription revenue outside the price war; it refuses dealers and broad model ranges.
deliver.activities_takeaway: Software and gigafactories carry the strategy; direct sales and charging support them.
reinforcement: More cars → more fleet data → better FSD → more subscription revenue → funds scale and price cuts → more cars
misaligned: An aging, narrow model lineup works against volume while BYD launches cheaper models
Repeated price cuts erode the WTP the software is meant to build
judgment: Partly organized: software and manufacturing are strong; the product pipeline lags rivals
deliver.takeaway: The system depends on one thing: autonomy arriving before car margins erode further.

activities.activity: In-house software, FSD and OTA updates
activities.define_link: Tech-forward buyers wanting a car that improves
activities.create_link: Raises WTP via FSD and new features
activities.capture_link: Subscription revenue outside the price war

activities.define_link: Buyers wanting a simple online purchase

activities.capture_link: Rivals' drivers pay Tesla to charge
Diversifies away from auto rivalry (46.7 GWh, +49%)

not_do: No dealer network or paid advertising (gives up local reach and marketing)
No broad model range (gives up segments like cheap compacts and trucks at scale)

define: **Who:** tech-forward EV buyers, plus utilities buying storage
**Problem solved:** static gas cars and EVs with weak software or charging
create: **WTP vs. cost:** cost wedge vs legacy makers; WTP from software
**Positioning map:** on the frontier, squeezed from below by BYD
**VRI:** software loop and scale temporary; sustained only if autonomy works
capture: **Six forces:** rivalry and price-sensitive buyers are strongest
**Power:** beats legacy rivals on cost; no edge over BYD
